## [Note]

- MHA-Go now requires `manager_ip` to be one of `slave_ips` and defaults to the last configured replica, keeping the failover controller outside the primary failure domain. Review custom MHA-Go inventory overrides before upgrading.
- The default MHA-Go salvage policy is now `availability-first`. It can promote the most advanced surviving replica when the old primary host is unreachable, but transactions that never reached any replica cannot be recovered. Select `strict` or `salvage-if-possible` when that tradeoff is not acceptable.
- The ClickHouse `default` user no longer trusts `::/0`. Deployments now trust loopback and the exact ClickHouse node addresses from inventory by default; add required client IPs or CIDRs through `clickhouse_default_user_allowed_networks`.
- `setup_nfs_server.yml` is a lab/test helper only. Production backup storage must use an externally managed NFS service and security policy.

## [Add]

- Add automatic rollback to `dbbotctl release upgrade` for failures after snapshot creation, including failure-phase metadata, rollback validation, history records, and regression coverage.
- Add protected, root-owned ClickHouse automation client configuration so backup, restore, validation, and deployment checks do not expose passwords in process arguments.
- Add ClickHouse complex-password XML rendering and command-line credential safety regression coverage.
- Add MHA-Go VIP lifecycle controls, including initial primary placement, stale-manager cleanup, persisted VIP state, dedicated manager-to-node SSH credentials, a forced-command allowlist, post-deploy verification, and complete uninstall cleanup.
- Add SHA-256 verification of ClickHouse configuration snapshot archives before restore extraction.

## [Change]

- Replace broad classic MHA and MHA-Go sudo permissions with validated, command-specific policies under `/etc/sudoers.d`, and remove legacy dbbot-generated rules from `/etc/sudoers`.
- Enable Group Replication members to start Group Replication on boot and keep Group Replication deployments read-only until initial provisioning is ready, improving safe automatic rejoin after `mysqld` restarts.
- Escape ClickHouse passwords in generated XML, protect credential-bearing cluster and client files with mode `0600`, and suppress sensitive Ansible task output.
- Make ClickHouse uninstall stop failures fatal and refuse configuration, data, log, or ZooKeeper deletion while the managed service or matching process is still running.
- Change the lab NFS export directory defaults to mode `0770` and numeric ownership `18123:18123`, matching the default ClickHouse runtime account.
- Restrict `alertmanager.yml` to mode `0600` because it can contain SMTP credentials and other notification secrets.

## [Fix]

- Fix MHA-Go deployments so the manager survives primary-host failure, VIP SSH is established and verified before failover, the VIP starts on the configured primary, stale VIP artifacts are removed safely, and unsafe remote commands are rejected.
- Fix classic MHA VIP validation and cleanup by validating interface and netmask values, checking the complete sudoers configuration, and verifying required and denied commands.
- Fix failed release upgrades leaving a partially replaced installation when a valid rollback snapshot is available.
- Pin the ClickHouse credential-rendering regression to the portable Ansible controller interpreter so it runs consistently on Ubuntu GitHub runners.
